sections.title: The letter Ä
paragraphs: The letter name is (Ä) /ɛː/. Its main sound is a vowel. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. You hear it in (Äpfel) /ˈɛpfəl/, which means apples. This letter makes two sounds in German.

sections.title: How to speak it
paragraphs: For the first sound, open your mouth halfway. Spread your lips slightly. Keep the tongue flat and push it slightly forward. Say a short vowel. For the second sound, keep the same mouth shape, but hold the vowel for more time. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: You make the short vowel in a short, closed stressed syllable. A stressed syllable is one you say with more strength. You hear this sound in (Hände) /ˈhɛndə/. You hold a long vowel in an open syllable or before one consonant. A long sound is one you hold for more time. You hear this sound in (Käse) /ˈkɛːzə/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not turn the long vowel into a diphthong. A diphthong is two vowel sounds that glide together. English words like bear or care glide at the end. Keep your mouth still and hold one steady sound. Do not make the short vowel too open like the sound in cat. Make it closer to the vowel in bed.
